kept.excerpt: France beat Paraguay 1-0 in the World Cup round of 16, with Kylian Mbappe converting a 70th-minute penalty after Desire Doue was fouled. Mbappe rejoined Lionel Messi as the tournament’s joint-top scorer with seven goals. France advanced to a quarter-final against Morocco.
kept.publisher: Agence France-Presse, via The Philippine Star
kept.relevance: The latest included scoring-race report establishes that Messi faced a joint leader on seven goals, with both players still in the competition.

kept.excerpt: Messi scored his seventh goal of the tournament as Argentina overcame Cabo Verde 3-2 after extra time to reach the last 16. Argentina struggled against Cabo Verde’s defensive organisation and physical strength, and several players suffered cramp or exhaustion. Egypt awaited Argentina in the next round.
kept.relevance: FIFA confirms Messi’s seven-goal tally and Argentina’s continued participation while documenting the physical demands and elimination risk affecting his remaining scoring opportunities.

kept.excerpt: Messi scored in the 29th minute of Argentina’s 3-2 extra-time victory over Cape Verde, extending his scoring streak to eight consecutive World Cup games. His seven tournament goals put him one ahead of Mbappé at the time of this report. FIFA’s scoring-leader tiebreakers were assists first and fewest minutes played second.
kept.relevance: This dated report provides Messi’s immediate scoring position and explains the FIFA tiebreakers relevant to determining the official leader.

kept.excerpt: Egypt advanced past Australia after a 1-1 draw and a 4-2 penalty-shootout victory. Egypt remained unbeaten and secured a round-of-16 match in Atlanta on July 7 against the winner of Argentina versus Cabo Verde.
kept.relevance: The official report establishes the next opponent and scheduled match date underlying Messi’s next potential scoring opportunity.

kept.excerpt: Messi came off the bench to score as Argentina beat Jordan 3-1 for a third consecutive Group J victory. Lionel Scaloni made nine changes from the lineup that beat Austria. Giovani Lo Celso, Lautaro Martinez and Messi scored Argentina’s goals, and Messi became the first player to score in seven consecutive World Cup finals matches.
kept.relevance: This report documents Messi’s scoring form and Argentina’s use of squad rotation, which affects his playing time and scoring exposure.

kept.excerpt: Kylian Mbappé finished the 2022 World Cup as its top scorer with eight goals and received the adidas Golden Boot. Lionel Messi won the adidas Golden Ball as Argentina lifted the World Cup trophy. The tournament produced 172 goals, surpassing the previous record of 171.
kept.relevance: The preceding World Cup supplies an official historical scoring benchmark and identifies Mbappé as an established Golden Boot competitor.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-06. Included six items with explicit publication dates visible in web-search results, prioritising FIFA and dated AP, Reuters and AFP reporting. Excerpts are factual paraphrases of the retrieved source text. Full-page web_fetch failed because of provider configuration; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned a rate-limit error, so verification relied on dated search-result text. Excluded undated live statistics, betting and prediction-market material, later publications, and pages whose retrieved bodies contained post-cutoff updates despite an earlier original publication date. The July 3 AP scoring position is historical to that report; the July 6 AFP item supplies the more recent included comparison. No forecast probability or tournament outcome is included.
